name: Field Doctor-Style Chilli Con Carne (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
520 g Extra Lean Beef
520 g Whole grain rice
1 x 400 g tin Plum Tomato
240 g Black Beans
2 medium Carrots
1 1/4 Green Peppers
1 medium Courgette
1/2 Red Peppers
1 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
3 tbsp Coriander
1 1/2 tbsp Smoked Paprika
3 tbsp Mixed Herbs
1 1/4 tbsp Cumin Ground
1 tsp Tamari [water, SOYA beans, sea salt]
1 tsp Beef Stock [Beef Extract, Water, Salt]
1 1/4 tsp Tapioca Starch
2/3 tsp Sea Salt
1/3 tsp Celery Salt (CELERY)
1 tsp Chipotle chilli
1/2 tsp Cinnamon Ground
1/2 tsp Oregano
directions:
1. Rice: Cook wholegrain rice; drain and keep warm.

2. Brown beef: Fry extra-lean beef in extra virgin olive oil until browned.

3. Chilli: Add carrot, green pepper, red pepper and courgette; cook until softening. Stir in cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, cinnamon, chipotle, chopped tomato, tomato puree, black beans, beef stock, tamari, celery salt and water. Simmer 25–30 minutes until thick; tapioca slurry if needed. Season with sea salt.

4. Serve over rice with coriander.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Water, Extra Lean Beef, Whole grain rice, Chopped Tomato, Black Beans, Carrot, Green Pepper, Courgette...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chilli Con Carne (Low FODMAP) (~403 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/chilli-con-carne
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~403 g x 8 = 3224 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~518 g (inferred ~16.08% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~58 g (inferred ~1.80% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
